# AC Server Manager 0.5.2 Preview

## Changes

This preview includes the changes developed since 0.4.1.

- Double-click a car name in **Cars and slots** to view its description, available specifications, skin icons and preview. Apply a skin to the selected slot, or cancel without changing it.
- Right-click a stopped server to **Delete server** or **Rename folder…**. Deletion uses the Windows Recycle Bin and asks for confirmation. Renaming preserves files, backups, drafts and the separate in-game server name. Running servers remain protected.
- Choose your own servers folder and keep it across application updates. Detect Assetto Corsa through Steam libraries, with manual selection available. Paths and language are saved in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ACServerManager\settings.json`; older preferences are imported when needed.
- Recover the saved Content Manager path and detect running, registered or commonly installed portable copies. Launch Content Manager from its own folder.
- Save directly, with success shown in the status bar and validation notices in the Validation tab. Keep the server list, selection and editor stable during saving.
- Skip writes and backups when configuration and content are unchanged, including edits reverted to their original values. Keep protection against external configuration edits and allow preparation of missing server content.
- Read older Kunos car, skin and track metadata in Windows-1252 and Unicode BOM encodings without changing game files.
- Use consistent **#FF5D43** orange accents, themed server menus and compact search fields with aligned hints and input cursors.

## Download and run

Extract **ACServerManager-0.5.2-preview-win-x64.zip** completely into a writable folder and run **AssettoServerManager.exe**. The Windows x64 package includes .NET; keep the other files alongside the EXE. `SHA256SUMS.txt` contains the archive checksum.

Bring your own game content and Content Manager. Existing servers stay in your chosen folder. Saving does not restart a running server. The car dialog uses installed skin images rather than a 3D showroom.

Application: MIT; bundled runtime notices are in `licenses/`.
